meta.title: Rezolve AI — Daniel Wagner's Brain Suite generative-commerce platform from the 2024 NASDAQ listing through Microsoft, Google, and Tether partnerships
meta.abstract: Rezolve AI Limited (NASDAQ: RZLV) is a UK-headquartered generative-AI commerce platform — its Brain Suite (Brain Commerce, Brain Checkout, Brain Engage, Brain Assistant) targets retailers seeking to embed conversational AI across discovery, checkout, and customer engagement. Founded and led by Daniel Wagner, Rezolve listed on NASDAQ via SPAC merger with Armada Acquisition Corp. in August 2024. Strategic narrative through 2024-2026 has centered on partner-led distribution through Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Tether (the stablecoin issuer made a strategic equity investment in 2024-2025), plus large-customer pilot conversions in retail and quick-service restaurant verticals.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
## Partner-Led at NASDAQ Altitude

When Rezolve AI Limited closed its business combination with Armada Acquisition Corp. I on 15 August 2024 and its ordinary shares began trading on NASDAQ as RZLV the following morning, the company was carrying consolidated annual revenues of just $2.01 million. What it carried in greater abundance was a structural thesis: that a generative-AI commerce platform embedded inside the distribution networks of Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud — and underpinned by a strategic equity stake from Tether, the world's largest stablecoin issuer — could convert a global pipeline of large retailers into recurring SaaS revenue at a pace unavailable to earlier-generation competitors. That thesis became the defining commercial narrative of the post-SPAC period and remained its principal subject of investor scrutiny through the dossier's frozen-snapshot date of 23 May 2026.

Rezolve AI is domiciled in the United Kingdom, headquartered in London, and files annual results on Form 20-F as a foreign private issuer on the SEC's EDGAR system. Daniel Wagner has served as chief executive since June 2016, and Rezolve's own management materials continued to frame his prior operating record around MAID and Venda, the enterprise e-commerce platform sold to Oracle in 2014. [Rezolve 2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm) [Rezolve Management Team](https://investor.rezolve.com/corporate-governance/management-team)

## Brain Suite: The Product Architecture

Rezolve's commercial platform, **Brain Suite**, comprises four modules: Brain Commerce (product discovery and semantic search), Brain Checkout (conversational checkout and payments), Brain Engage (loyalty and retention), and Brain Assistant (retail AI agent). The platform targets large retailers, quick-service restaurant operators, and e-commerce marketplaces through a SaaS subscription model layered with transaction and engagement fees. (See the Platform chapter for detailed product architecture.)

## Revenue Inflection: From $2 Million to a $232 Million Exit Run Rate

The financial trajectory from NASDAQ listing through year-end 2025 was striking in velocity. Full-year 2024 consolidated revenue was $2.013567 million and net loss was $173.451133 million. In the company's later 2025 annual report, the comparative year-end 2024 cash balance was $9.73 million. The [2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm) and the later comparative disclosures in [Architecting Agentic Commerce](https://investor.rezolve.com/static-files/6f81887f-0aee-4363-afd5-11a0d12d0acd) preserved the central point: auditors and management said substantial doubt existed about the company's ability to continue as a going concern absent further financing.

The pivot into 2025 was steep. Full-year 2025 revenue reached $46.8 million, with second-half revenue of $40.5 million against $6.3 million in the first half. On 30 March 2026 the company said it had exited 2025 with $19.4 million of December MRR and a $232 million-plus ARR run rate, well ahead of the original $100 million year-end objective; on 30 April 2026 it said first-quarter 2026 revenue reached $60 million. [FY2025 results release](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html) [Q1 2026 update](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-delivers-60-million-q1-2026-revenue-exceeding-full/)

| Period | Revenue | Net Loss |
|--------|---------|----------|
| FY2023 | $145K | — |
| FY2024 | $2.01M | $173.5M |
| FY2025 | ~$46.8M | $101.4M |
| Q1 2026 | ~$60.0M | — |

*Sources: [Rezolve 2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm); [Rezolve FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html); [Rezolve Q1 2026 update](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-delivers-60-million-q1-2026-revenue-exceeding-full/); [Architecting Agentic Commerce](https://investor.rezolve.com/static-files/6f81887f-0aee-4363-afd5-11a0d12d0acd)*

## Three Strategic Anchors

The partner-led distribution strategy rested on three relationships: **Microsoft Azure** (Brain Suite on Azure infrastructure, $130 million in co-sell commitment), **Google Cloud** (reseller arrangement potentially accounting for half of AI commerce revenue at scale), and **Tether** (strategic equity investment plus stablecoin-payments integration). The April 2025 Liverpool Mexico contract validated the Google relationship, with Brain Commerce's SEO Studio integrated with Google's search ecosystem. [Microsoft-Rezolve partnership](https://news.microsoft.com/source/2024/10/03/microsoft-and-rezolve-ai-partner-to-drive-global-retail-innovation-with-ai-powered-commerce-solutions/) [Google-Rezolve partnership](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-and-google-sign-strategic-partnership-revolutionize/) [Liverpool Mexico contract](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-secures-98-million-annual-contract-liverpool-mexico)

> "2024 has been a game-changing year for Rezolve Ai. Our strategic partnerships with Microsoft, Google, and exciting crypto and payments initiative with Tether are unlocking unprecedented opportunities."
> — Daniel Wagner, [December 2024 year-end statement](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-closes-2024-transformational-milestones-bolstered)

## Customer Scale

The most publicly detailed customer win was a [$9.8 million annual contract](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-secures-98-million-annual-contract-liverpool-mexico) with Liverpool Mexico, announced on 15 April 2025. By 16 December 2025 Rezolve said it served more than 650 enterprise clients; by 30 March 2026 it said the platform had passed 950 enterprise customers, processed 112.7 billion API calls, and reached 59.8 million consumer devices. [December 2025 trading update](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-shatters-year-end-expectations-december-revenue) [FY2025 results release](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html)

## The Dossier's Open Questions

Five questions structure the analysis that follows. First: whether the $232 million ARR exit rate represented durable contracted revenue or was partly flattered by implementation timing and billings concentration. Second: the specific commercial terms governing the Microsoft and Google arrangements and the unit economics per hyperscaler-referred lead. Third: the competitive frame against Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Shopify Plus, and Adobe Commerce — all of which hold larger installed bases and deeper systems-integration ecosystems — and whether Brain Suite's generative-AI architecture is genuinely differentiated or replicable by better-capitalised incumbents. Fourth: what Wagner's prior track record implies for execution against a stated $500 million ARR target for 2026. Fifth: with an accumulated deficit of $359.6 million, current liabilities of $262.1 million against current assets of $175.0 million, and year-end shareholders' equity of $246.8 million at fiscal year-end 2025, whether the revenue trajectory translates into durable shareholder value or is consumed by capital-structure complexity and working-capital strain.

chapters.title: From 2016 founding through 2024 SPAC merger to partner-led scaling
chapters.body:
When Rezolve AI Limited began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker RZLV on 16 August 2024, Daniel Wagner became, by his own account, a two-time Nasdaq chief executive — the first occasion having been nearly thirty years earlier, when his online-information company MAID listed as Dialog in 1995. The symmetry was not incidental. Wagner has spent four decades building platforms that aggregate and monetise data at commercial scale; Rezolve AI is his most ambitious attempt to fuse that institutional instinct with generative artificial intelligence and make it the operating layer of global retail.

## A Serial Founder's Calculus

The biographical arc matters for how investors and enterprise customers assess the venture. Wagner dropped out of school at sixteen to work as a shop assistant for Julian Richer at Richer Sounds, the British consumer-electronics chain. His first company, MAID (Market Analysis Information Database), was conceived at twenty, while he was working in advertising: an online database of business intelligence that was among the first commercially networked information services in Britain. Founded in 1984, MAID listed on the London Stock Exchange in 1994 and moved to Nasdaq the following year as Dialog, where Wagner became one of the youngest chief executives of a publicly traded company. The business was eventually sold to Thomson Reuters.

His second major venture, Venda, was founded in 1998, capitalising on the wreckage of the first dot-com cycle. Rezolve's own management page said the platform later ran major retail websites including Lands' End, Tesco, Boohoo, TJX Companies and Neiman Marcus before its sale to Oracle in 2014. [Rezolve Management Team](https://investor.rezolve.com/corporate-governance/management-team) The same year, Attraqt, a product-discovery software company Wagner had co-founded in 2003, listed on AIM; he stepped down as chairman in June 2016.

Wagner's final pre-Rezolve venture, Powa Technologies, was the cautionary counterweight in the ledger. Official UK records show that Powa Technologies Group plc entered administration on 19 February 2016, and the officers register for Powa Technologies Limited shows Daniel Wagner and several other directors resigning the same day. [Companies House – Powa insolvency](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/08389133/insolvency) [Companies House – Powa officers](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/06376989/officers) Wagner founded Rezolve later the same year — the product architecture carried clear thematic continuity with Powa's original vision, though the new company would pursue it with a different capital structure and, eventually, a different distribution model.

## Building the Commerce Brain, 2016–2024

Rezolve was incorporated in the United Kingdom in 2016 and spent its pre-listing years developing what it would eventually brand the Brain Suite — a family of modular generative-AI tools targeted at large retailers, quick-service restaurant operators, and e-commerce marketplaces. The suite eventually comprised four commercial products: Brain Commerce (semantic product search, generative product Q&A, personalised discovery), Brain Checkout (conversational checkout and payments orchestration), Brain Engage (loyalty, post-purchase retention, and customer lifecycle management), and Brain Assistant (a general-purpose retail AI assistant). Underpinning all four modules is brainpowa, the company's proprietary large language model tuned specifically for retail inference — the component that differentiates the platform from generic cloud-AI wrappers and that ultimately attracted Microsoft and Google as infrastructure partners rather than competitive alternatives.

The revenue model was designed around a SaaS subscription per merchant layered with variable engagement and transaction fees. Rezolve's stated thesis was that the largest global retailers would pay for a unified AI commerce layer rather than build one internally. By the time the company sought a public listing, its SEC filings described active pilots with multiple top-100 global retail brands, though converting those pilots to contracted recurring revenue remained the central commercial test at the moment the SPAC transaction closed.

## The Armada Transaction

Armada Acquisition Corp. I was a blank-cheque vehicle that had raised capital from public investors with the stated mandate to merge with a technology company. Armada stockholders approved the transaction at a special meeting held on 1 August 2024. The closing followed on 15 August 2024, and Rezolve's ordinary shares and warrants were expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under the symbols RZLV and RZLVW on 16 August 2024, with Armada folded into the combined entity as a wholly owned subsidiary. [Business-combination closing release](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-limited-closes-business-combination-armada-0/) [Post-closing SEC filing](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8341/html)

The post-merger capital structure reflected the mechanics typical of de-SPAC transactions executed in a constrained financing environment. By year-end 2024 Rezolve said about $59 million of variable-rate debt had been converted to equity, reducing the cash-interest burden, and it had also priced a $15 million registered offering. [Rezolve debt-conversion release](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-converts-59-million-variable-rate-convertible-loans) [Rezolve $15 million offering](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-announces-pricing-15-million-registered-offering/) The combined entity files as a Foreign Private Issuer on SEC EDGAR, submitting its annual report on Form 20-F and interim disclosures on Form 6-K rather than the domestic 10-K and 10-Q cadence, a distinction that affects both disclosure timelines and the level of segmental detail available to the public market.

That sequencing mattered. It meant Rezolve entered 2025 not merely as a freshly listed former SPAC target but as a company that had already used the public market to simplify debt, raise growth capital and buy time for the commercial thesis to prove itself.

The post-listing executive team placed operational depth alongside Wagner's founding mandate. Sauvik Banerjjee served as CEO of Technology and Product; Dr. Salman Ahmed as Chief Technology Officer; and Richard Burchill as Chief Financial Officer. Wagner retained the chairmanship and chief-executive title, preserving the founder-led governance structure that had characterised the pre-listing company.

## Three Strategic Anchors

The ninety days following the Nasdaq listing produced three partnership announcements that, taken together, defined the go-to-market architecture Rezolve AI intended to scale.

On [3 October 2024](https://news.microsoft.com/source/2024/10/03/microsoft-and-rezolve-ai-partner-to-drive-global-retail-innovation-with-ai-powered-commerce-solutions/), Microsoft and Rezolve AI announced a five-year strategic partnership with a $130 million joint go-to-market commitment. Nick Parker, Microsoft's President of Industry and Partnerships, said Rezolve's technology was "specifically designed for commerce and retail, transforming how businesses approach customer engagement."

Six weeks later, on [20 November 2024](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-and-google-sign-strategic-partnership-revolutionize/), Google Cloud formalised a reseller arrangement with an unusual spend-pass-through: customers could apply existing Google Cloud commitments toward Brain Suite licences. The channel was projected to account for more than 50% of Rezolve's revenues over the following years. Google's engineers committed to collaborate on Brain Suite development, with disclosed exploration of integration into Search, Maps, Android, and YouTube.

On [4 December 2024](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/tether-and-rezolve-ai-share-vision-make-crypto-mainstream), Rezolve announced Tether's Wallet Development Kit integration into Brain Checkout — instant crypto-to-fiat conversion eliminating conventional merchant-processing fees. By late February 2025 the company had paired that payments strategy with a [$1 billion bitcoin-treasury programme](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-launches-groundbreaking-1-billion-bitcoin-treasury/) starting with a planned $100 million initial investment, after also entering a securities purchase agreement disclosed on Form 6-K. [Rezolve Feb. 25 2025 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/static-files/db718f57-b393-4aef-a015-179b00cb0d4a)

As the dossier's frozen snapshot of 23 May 2026 approached, the question that had been present at listing remained the dominant frame: whether the cohort of named top-100 global retail brands cycling through Brain Suite pilots would complete the conversion to contracted, recurring SaaS revenue at the scale the partner-led distribution model required.

chapters.title: Brain Suite: Brain Commerce, Brain Checkout, Brain Engage, Brain Assistant
chapters.body:
## The Architecture of Generative Commerce

Rezolve's core commercial proposition rests on the claim that generative AI makes it possible to collapse the traditional retail technology stack — separate search vendors, checkout processors, loyalty platforms, customer-service tooling — into a unified, AI-native layer. The Brain Suite ships as four discrete but interconnected modules: Brain Commerce, Brain Checkout, Brain Engage, and Brain Assistant.

The suite was not assembled from acquisitions. All four modules share a common data layer, a common large-language-model inference layer, and a common retailer integration API — organic architectural coherence that positions Brain Suite as a plug-in intelligence fabric sitting above existing order-management and ERP systems rather than replacing them.

## Brain Commerce: Search Reimagined as Conversation

Brain Commerce addresses the entry point of the retail journey: product discovery. Traditional retail search returned keyword matches against a product catalogue. Generative search does something structurally different — it interprets intent, tolerates ambiguity, and responds with curated answers rather than ranked lists.

Within Brain Commerce, that manifests in three related capabilities. Semantic search uses dense vector embeddings of the product catalogue so that a query for "something warm for a rainy autumn walk" surfaces waterproof outerwear without the customer ever typing a category keyword. Generative product Q&A allows shoppers to ask freeform questions — "Is this sofa stain-resistant and does it come in under two metres wide?" — and receive answers synthesised from product specifications, reviews, and specification sheets rather than a redirect to a PDF. Product discovery feeds both into personalised homepages and into in-session recommendation rails that update based on conversational context accumulated across the session.

The value proposition for the retailer is measurable in terms that merchandising teams understand: reduced zero-results searches, higher add-to-cart rates from discovery sessions, and longer dwell times on product pages driven by conversational engagement rather than passive browsing. Wagner positioned Brain Commerce in investor communications as attacking the long tail of search queries that legacy keyword-matching systems fail — the statistic that roughly 15 to 20 per cent of any given day's search queries on a large retail site are queries that site has never seen before is a standard framing in commerce AI sales cycles, and Rezolve adopted it as a core proof-point.

## Brain Checkout: Conversation Through the Transaction

If Brain Commerce moves a shopper toward a product, Brain Checkout closes the loop. The module is built around conversational checkout — the ability to complete a purchase through a natural-language interface, including voice, chat widget, or AI-generated transactional SMS, without the customer navigating a multi-page checkout funnel.

The payments orchestration layer supports multiple payment rails: card-based schemes, digital wallets, and a stablecoin-integrated crypto-payment option enabled by the Tether partnership. Brain Checkout can route transactions settled in USDT through the same conversational checkout interface used for card payments. The near-term addressable market for stablecoin checkout at Western mass-market retailers remains limited; the more commercially significant dimension lies in markets with elevated card-payment friction — Southeast Asia, Latin America, parts of the Middle East.

For retailers, the financial case for Brain Checkout is cart-abandonment reduction. The multi-page checkout flow has historically been the largest single point of conversion loss in e-commerce, and conversational checkout — particularly on mobile — shortens the cognitive distance between decision and transaction. Rezolve disclosed that Brain Checkout is designed to integrate with existing payment gateways and order-management systems via API, preserving the retailer's existing commercial relationships with acquirers and processors rather than requiring a wholesale payments migration.

## Brain Engage: Retention in the Generative Era

The third module, Brain Engage, operates post-transaction. Its domain is the set of problems traditionally owned by CRM and loyalty vendors: keeping customers engaged with a brand between purchases, personalising communications, and reducing churn.

Brain Engage approaches these problems through the same LLM inference layer that powers Brain Commerce and Brain Checkout, which creates a material architectural advantage: the engagement signals from a shopper's conversational commerce sessions — what they searched for, what questions they asked, what alternatives they considered before buying — flow directly into the segmentation and personalisation logic that Brain Engage uses to generate outreach. A customer who asked detailed questions about a sofa's durability before purchasing it has revealed a preference signal that a traditional post-purchase email sequence, triggered only by transaction date and category, would never capture.

Practical outputs from Brain Engage include AI-generated push notifications calibrated to individual purchase-cycle patterns, conversational loyalty programme interactions where points balances and reward redemption are handled inside the same chat interface as product discovery, and dynamic re-engagement sequences that adapt messaging based on the conversational history accumulated across prior sessions. The retention use case is increasingly important to Rezolve's commercial thesis because it expands the addressable revenue per merchant: a retailer that deploys Brain Commerce and Brain Checkout has a clear ROI narrative tied to conversion rate; a retailer that also activates Brain Engage opens a second revenue stream for Rezolve in engagement-based fee structures layered above the base SaaS subscription.

## Brain Assistant: The In-Store and Service Layer

Brain Assistant completes the suite as a dual-mode AI assistant deployable for both customer-facing and store-associate-facing use cases. On the customer side it functions as an always-available service agent — handling returns queries, order status, product FAQs, and complaint triage — integrated into the same chat and voice interfaces used for commerce. On the associate side, it gives retail floor staff access to live inventory data, product knowledge, and customer history through a natural-language interface that does not require training on proprietary systems.

The associate-facing application is particularly relevant for quick-service restaurant operators, a customer segment Rezolve identified explicitly in its investor materials. QSR environments — high throughput, high staff turnover, multi-item order complexity — benefit significantly from an AI layer that reduces the training time required to bring new staff to competence on menu configurations, allergen protocols, and up-sell sequences.

## Cloud Architecture

Brain Suite is delivered cloud-native on both Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud. The dual-cloud architecture gives enterprise retailers a deployment path consistent with existing hyperscaler relationships — a material procurement consideration given that enterprise committees weigh existing spend commitments and consolidated billing arrangements.

## Revenue Model

Rezolve's revenue model has two layers: a SaaS subscription per merchant (scoped to modules deployed and volume tier) and usage-based fees tied to transaction or engagement volume.

| Module | Primary Value Driver | Fee Layer |
|---|---|---|
| Brain Commerce | Conversion rate from discovery | SaaS subscription |
| Brain Checkout | Cart abandonment reduction | SaaS + per-transaction |
| Brain Engage | Retention / repeat purchase rate | SaaS + per-engagement |
| Brain Assistant | Service cost reduction | SaaS subscription |

The blended revenue-per-merchant figure expands as retailers move from piloting a single module to deploying the full suite — the core land-and-expand mechanic embedded in Rezolve's commercial architecture.

chapters.title: Revenue trajectory, cash burn, capital structure, post-SPAC dynamics
chapters.body:
## From F-4 to NASDAQ: The Revenue Baseline at Listing

When Rezolve AI closed its business combination with Armada Acquisition Corp. I on 15 August 2024 and began trading on Nasdaq as RZLV the next morning, the business that entered the public market was still small by any conventional software metric. The FY2024 Form 20-F later showed revenue of only $145,000 in 2023 and $2.013567 million in 2024. That mismatch between current scale and public-market ambition was the essence of the transaction: investors were backing the conversion of a partner-led enterprise pipeline into recurring revenue, not a mature income statement already showing proof of scale. [Business-combination closing release](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-limited-closes-business-combination-armada-0/) [Rezolve 2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm)

That framing matters because Rezolve reported as a Foreign Private Issuer, using Form 20-F and Form 6-K rather than the domestic 10-K and 10-Q cadence. The company reported in U.S. dollars while keeping its principal executive office in London, and the filings described material exposure to sterling and euro operating costs. The public numbers therefore reflected not just commercial execution but a capital-intensive London-headquartered operating base being translated into Nasdaq-facing dollar accounts. [Rezolve 2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm) [FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html)

## Revenue Trajectory: FY2023–FY2025

Rezolve's revenue model was always going to look lumpy in the early years. Brain Suite contracts bundled subscriptions, implementation, platform access and usage-linked elements, which meant that even named customer wins did not necessarily show up at once in recognised revenue. The FY2024 20-F captured the pre-inflection phase: $2.013567 million of revenue, $173.451133 million of net loss, and auditors and management both warning that substantial doubt existed about the group's ability to continue as a going concern without further financing. [Rezolve 2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm)

By the March 2026 reporting cycle the shape of the P&L had changed materially. Rezolve reported FY2025 revenue of $46.800099 million, with $40.5 million of that in the second half against $6.3 million in the first half. December 2025 revenue alone reached $19.4 million, which management translated into a $232 million-plus ARR exit rate. Net loss narrowed to $101.410228 million, still heavy in absolute terms but no longer telling the same story as the 2024 filing. [FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html)

| Period | Revenue | Net loss | Net cash used in operating activities |
|---|---|---|---|
| FY2024 | $2.013567M | $173.451133M | $22.382670M |
| FY2025 | $46.800099M | $101.410228M | $63.147255M |

The cost structure also became more legible in 2025. Cost of revenue was $15.922202 million, sales and marketing expense was $12.062375 million, research and development expense was $11.198074 million, and general and administrative expense was still by far the largest line at $90.366226 million. That mix made clear that Rezolve had not yet become a lightweight software annuity; it was still paying for public-company infrastructure, acquisitions, integration and commercial build-out while trying to prove the operating leverage embedded in the Brain Suite model. [FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html)

## Cash Burn and Operating Cash Flow

The cash-flow statement showed how expensive that transition remained. Net cash used in operating activities was $22.382670 million in 2024 and widened to $63.147255 million in 2025. Net cash used in investing activities rose to $24.708239 million in 2025 as the company spent on intangible assets, digital assets and acquisitions. In other words, the revenue inflection arrived alongside a larger operating and investing cash appetite, not in place of it. [Rezolve 2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm) [FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html)

The balance sheet captured the same tension. Cash and cash equivalents rose to $111.112251 million at 31 December 2025 from $9.729546 million a year earlier, but current liabilities also climbed to $262.072900 million against current assets of $174.950749 million. Accumulated deficit widened to $359.619973 million even as shareholders' equity swung positive to $246.815532 million. The company had plainly become better capitalised; it had not become simple. [FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html)

Those liabilities were concentrated in a handful of large buckets rather than diffuse operating accruals. At year-end 2025 the company carried $102.142933 million of short-term debt, $46.500843 million of deferred revenue, $27.772675 million of current contingent consideration, $35.714363 million of accounts payable and $50.092029 million of long-term debt. The asset side, meanwhile, had become acquisition-heavy: goodwill stood at $168.396367 million and intangible assets at $239.200952 million. That balance sheet was consistent with a company trying to consolidate a category at speed, but it also meant that execution risk was inseparable from integration risk. [FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html)

The going-concern language therefore remained central rather than vestigial. The FY2024 20-F had tied that warning to recurring losses and negative operating cash flow. The March 2026 materials argued that the capital position had improved sharply, with management saying more than $750 million of total funding had been secured and no additional operational equity was needed for the 2026 plan, yet the filing record still forced investors to weigh growth against structure. [Rezolve 2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm) [FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html)

## Capital Structure: Equity, Warrants and Strategic Money

The capital structure that emerged from the SPAC merger remained layered in the familiar post-2021 pattern: ordinary shares, public warrants, sponsor-linked paper, acquisition consideration, and repeated follow-on financing. Rezolve reported 208,260,754 ordinary shares issued and outstanding at 31 December 2024; by 31 December 2025 that figure had risen to 336,327,587. The company still carried a warrant liability of $718,625 at the latter date. Dilution was not a hypothetical risk embedded in the documents; it was visible in the year-on-year share count. [Rezolve 2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm) [Rezolve 2025 Form 20-F excerpt](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8796/html) [FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html)

Three transactions illustrated the mechanism. First, on 19 December 2024 the company priced a $15 million registered offering of 5 million ordinary shares, or pre-funded warrants in lieu thereof, together with 5 million warrants, at $3.00 per unit. Second, on 21 February 2025 it entered into a securities purchase agreement covering convertible notes and related warrants. Third, in January 2026 the company agreed to issue 62.5 million ordinary shares in a financing that management later described as a $250 million oversubscribed raise. Each step improved liquidity while also widening the fully diluted capital base. [Rezolve $15 million offering](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-announces-pricing-15-million-registered-offering/) [Rezolve Feb. 25 2025 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/static-files/db718f57-b393-4aef-a015-179b00cb0d4a) [Rezolve 2025 Form 20-F excerpt](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8796/html)

Acquisition consideration added another layer of future dilution or cash claims. The same FY2025 statements that showed the enlarged share count also carried $27.772675 million of current contingent consideration and $23.277895 million of non-current contingent consideration, alongside ordinary shares payable of $10.660000 million. That meant investors were not only underwriting operating performance; they were also underwriting management's ability to integrate acquired assets and settle purchase obligations without compromising the balance sheet it had just rebuilt. [FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html)

The Tether relationship added a strategic layer rather than a purely financial one. Public disclosures described it as a combination of equity support and commercial integration around Brain Checkout and digital-asset settlement. What the filings available through the frozen window did not do was itemise a precise Tether shareholding, which meant investors could see the partnership's strategic importance more clearly than its exact place in the cap table. [Tether and Rezolve WDK announcement](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/tether-and-rezolve-ai-share-vision-make-crypto-mainstream) [Rezolve 2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm)

| Capital layer | Nature | Source document |
|---|---|---|
| Armada business combination | Public-market listing and initial post-closing equity structure | Closing release / 20-F |
| Public and sponsor warrants | Post-combination warrant overhang | 20-F / 2025 annual report |
| December 2024 registered offering | 5 million shares and 5 million warrants at $3.00 per unit | December 19, 2024 offering release |
| February 2025 securities purchase agreement | Convertible notes and related warrants | February 25, 2025 6-K |
| January 2026 equity financing | 62.5 million ordinary shares | 2025 annual report |
| Tether strategic investment | Equity support linked to payments integration | December 4, 2024 company release / 20-F |

## Cash Position, Runway and the Real Question

The financial question by the frozen snapshot date was not whether Rezolve had reached a revenue inflection; it had. The question was whether the revenue line could outrun the complexity of the capital structure and the working-capital demands that accompanied rapid deployment, acquisition activity and deferred-revenue build. Management's answer in spring 2026 was emphatic: the company said it had sufficient capital, more than $232 million of contracted revenue, and a path to a $360 million 2026 revenue target without new operational equity. [FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html)

Investors still had to decide how much of that answer was operating proof and how much was balance-sheet choreography. Rezolve had moved from a $2.0 million revenue company to a $46.8 million revenue company in a single reported year, but it had done so while issuing stock, converting debt, buying assets and carrying liabilities that remained large relative to current assets. The bull case rested on revenue conversion and margin leverage continuing faster than dilution and capital-structure complexity accumulated. That remained the decisive financial debate at 23 May 2026.

What distinguished Rezolve from many other post-SPAC software names was that the financial story could not be read in isolation from the commercial architecture. If Microsoft and Google really were compressing enterprise sales cycles and if contracted revenue really was converting into recognised revenue on the cadence management outlined, then the 2025 accounts might read in hindsight like the last structurally messy year before operating leverage emerged. If not, the same accounts offered enough evidence to support a harsher reading: that capital raises, acquisition accounting and revenue annualisation metrics were outrunning the slower work of building a dependable public-company software business. The filings through 23 May 2026 left both interpretations open.

chapters.title: Quarterly cadence from August 2024 listing through customer-pipeline conversion narrative
chapters.body:
## Debut on Nasdaq and the Architecture of Disclosure

When trading in Rezolve AI Limited's ordinary shares opened on the Nasdaq Global Market on 16 August 2024 under the ticker RZLV, the company's public narrative had already been written in advance. Two weeks earlier, Armada Acquisition Corp. I shareholders had voted to approve the business combination; the de-SPAC mechanics — PIPE investors, warrant structure, the conversion of Armada's trust — were baked into the F-4 prospectus filed with the SEC months before the first trade. What remained unwritten, in every meaningful commercial sense, was the revenue line. Full-year 2024 GAAP revenue would end at $2.013567 million, a figure the company's own annual reporting would characterise alongside a going-concern qualification from its auditors — a candid acknowledgement, standard for post-SPAC technology issuers of this vintage, that cash consumption and operating losses were outpacing near-term receipts. Net loss for 2024 reached $173.451133 million. [Rezolve 2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm) [Architecting Agentic Commerce](https://investor.rezolve.com/static-files/6f81887f-0aee-4363-afd5-11a0d12d0acd)

Daniel Wagner, retaining the founder's equity stake he had accumulated since Rezolve's 2016 incorporation, framed the moment as a beginning rather than a performance. "We are thrilled to have successfully completed the business combination with Armada and begin our next chapter," he said at listing. The corporate disclosure rhythm changed with it: as a Foreign Private Issuer on the SEC's EDGAR system, Rezolve was obliged to file 20-F annual reports and 6-K current reports — not 10-K and 10-Q forms — a cadence that would become the primary instrument through which investors read the company's quarterly story.

## October–November 2024: The Partner Sequence

The commercial architecture materialised in rapid succession. On 3 October, Microsoft announced a multi-year strategic partnership with $130 million in go-to-market support and access to 35,000 incentivised Microsoft sellers. On 20 November, Google Cloud formalised a reseller arrangement projected to generate more than 50% of Rezolve's forecast revenues. (Partnership details in the Customers & Partners chapter.) The two announcements, within seven weeks of each other, recast Rezolve's positioning from direct enterprise sales to distribution embedded within two of the world's largest cloud vendors.

## The FY2024 Earnings Release

Rezolve reported its full-year 2024 results on 24 April 2025, with the conference call following on 28 April. Full-year 2024 GAAP revenue of $2.0 million against a net loss of $173.5 million reflected not only operating expenditure but non-cash burdens typical of post-SPAC structures: warrant re-measurements, stock compensation, and public-company compliance costs. [FY2024 results release](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-smashes-past-50-billion-gmv-explosive-start-2025-over)

On the April 2025 call, Wagner and CFO Richard Burchill noted the average deal size in the pipeline had grown larger than initially modelled — a consequence attributed to Microsoft and Google co-sell channels routing larger retail counterparties into Rezolve's sales process.

## Scaling Into 2025: GroupBy and the First Major Customer Win

The year began with a structural expansion. On 11 February 2025, Rezolve announced the acquisition of GroupBy — an AI-powered site search and digital merchandising provider whose technology powered more than $30 billion in annual retail sales for its customers — in an all-equity transaction disclosed in its purchase agreement as 3,999,902 Rezolve shares to the sellers. The deal closed on 25 March 2025. Wagner called it "a transformative milestone," noting GroupBy's track record of driving $30 billion in annual retail sales for customers as evidence of the combined platform's commercial density. [Rezolve GroupBy acquisition announcement](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-acquire-groupby-strengthening-market-leadership) [GroupBy closing 6-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1920294/000095017025047916/groupby_closing_6-k.htm)

Six weeks later, on 15 April 2025, the company announced a $9.8 million annual contract with Liverpool Mexico — the largest single publicly disclosed customer win in company history. The contract covered Brain Commerce including an SEO Studio module integrated with Google's ecosystem — a proof-of-concept that a sophisticated large-format retailer, operating at national scale in a Google-covered market, had committed to the platform.

## The H1 2025 Reporting Cycle

On 1 October 2025, Rezolve released H1 2025 results: $6.3 million GAAP revenue (426% increase over H1 2024's $1.2 million). Gross margins on the software core exceeded 95%. More than 100 enterprise customers were live across retail, hospitality, and QSR categories, including Ferrero, H&M, Urban Outfitters, ASOS, Office Depot, and Rakuten Group.

Rezolve raised its 2025 ARR exit guidance to a minimum of $150 million and initiated a 2026 ARR exit target of $500 million.

## December Record and the Year-End Update

On 16 December 2025, Rezolve published a trading update ahead of the close of its fiscal year. December 2025 monthly revenue was expected to exceed $17 million, implying an annualised run rate above $200 million. The forecast ARR for the month was $209.88 million — more than double the $150 million floor the company had guided to three months earlier. The global enterprise customer count stood at more than 650. Adjusted EBITDA had turned positive. [December 2025 trading update](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-shatters-year-end-expectations-december-revenue)

Wagner on the milestone:

> "To go from a standing start to an expected ARR exceeding $200 million in just twelve months is exceptional."

The full-year figure, confirmed when the March 2026 6-K was filed, came in at $46.8 million of GAAP revenue — a roughly 23-fold multiple of 2024's $2.0 million. The second half accounted for $40.5 million of that total, a 543% step-up from the $6.3 million recorded in H1; the same March filing also lifted the year-end exit metric to $19.4 million of December MRR and a $232 million-plus ARR run rate. [March 2026 6-K / FY2025 results](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html)

| Period | GAAP Revenue | Key Metric |
|---|---|---|
| FY 2024 | $2.0 million | NASDAQ listing year; going-concern disclosed |
| H1 2025 | $6.3 million | +426% vs H1 2024 |
| H2 2025 | $40.5 million | +543% vs H1 2025 |
| FY 2025 | $46.8 million | $232M ARR exit rate |
| Q1 2026 | $60.0 million | Exceeds FY 2025 total in 90 days |

## Q1 2026: The Inflection Point

The first quarter of 2026, reported on 30 April 2026, produced preliminary unaudited revenue of $60 million — exceeding the entirety of the audited FY2025 figure within ninety days. The enterprise customer count had grown to more than 950. The company reiterated its $360 million revenue guidance for the full year 2026 while projecting a 2026 exit ARR above $500 million. Management stated that the 2026 plan and a path to profitability were achievable without additional equity raises — a direct response to the going-concern language that had followed the company since its 20-F filings. [Q1 2026 update](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-delivers-60-million-q1-2026-revenue-exceeding-full/)

> "Delivering $60 million of revenue in the first quarter is a major inflection point for Rezolve AI. Our focus is execution: converting our contracted base into revenue, scaling enterprise deployments."
> — Daniel M. Wagner, May 2026

The balance sheet told the tale of two structures operating in tension: $111.1 million in cash at 31 December 2025, current liabilities of $262.1 million against current assets of $175.0 million, and an accumulated deficit of $359.6 million even as the year-end shareholders' equity line had swung positive to $246.8 million. The 20-F for FY2025, filed in spring 2026, nevertheless repeated going-concern language even as the business was posting its fastest revenue growth. Against total funding raised since founding of more than $750 million, and 112.7 billion API calls processed in 2025 alone, the disclosure read as much like an accounting warning about structure and timing as a judgement on demand. [Architecting Agentic Commerce](https://investor.rezolve.com/static-files/6f81887f-0aee-4363-afd5-11a0d12d0acd) [FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html)

The pipeline-to-revenue conversion narrative Wagner had carried from the listing prospectus had, by the frozen snapshot date of 23 May 2026, produced its first verifiable acceleration. Whether the quarterly ramp — 90 days outpacing twelve months — would sustain through the second and third quarters of 2026 remained the central question for investors watching the cadence of each new 6-K.

---

**Sources:** [Rezolve Investor Relations](https://investor.rezolve.com) · [Rezolve 2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm) · [Architecting Agentic Commerce](https://investor.rezolve.com/static-files/6f81887f-0aee-4363-afd5-11a0d12d0acd) · [Microsoft Source — Microsoft/Rezolve partnership](https://news.microsoft.com/source/2024/10/03/microsoft-and-rezolve-ai-partner-to-drive-global-retail-innovation-with-ai-powered-commerce-solutions/) · [Rezolve GroupBy announcement](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-acquire-groupby-strengthening-market-leadership) · [Rezolve FY2024 results release](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-smashes-past-50-billion-gmv-explosive-start-2025-over) · [Rezolve H1 2025 results release](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-raises-2025-guidance-150m-arr-and-initiates-2026) · [Rezolve December 2025 trading update](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-shatters-year-end-expectations-december-revenue) · [Rezolve FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html) · [Rezolve Q1 2026 update](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-delivers-60-million-q1-2026-revenue-exceeding-full/)

chapters.title: Daniel Wagner, executive team, and the board
chapters.body:
## The founder's arc: from MAID to Rezolve

Daniel Maurice Wagner was born in Edgware, Middlesex, on 28 July 1963 and has spent four decades building, selling, and occasionally losing companies at the intersection of information technology and commerce. He left school at sixteen to work as a sales assistant at Julian Richer's hi-fi chain Richer Sounds, moved into advertising, and conceived a then-novel idea: packaging business databases as a subscription service for marketing professionals. In 1984, at the age of twenty, he founded Market Analysis Information Database — MAID — one of the earliest online information platforms, pre-dating the World Wide Web by half a decade and Amazon by more than a decade.

MAID grew to command what Wagner later described as 26 per cent of the global online information market, with 46 offices in 192 countries. It listed on the London Stock Exchange in 1994 and on NASDAQ in 1995, making Wagner one of the youngest CEOs of a dual-listed public company. The eventual acquirer was Thomson Reuters, which purchased M.A.I.D./Dialog in 2000 for approximately $500 million. The World Economic Forum selected Wagner as a Global Leader of Tomorrow, and Ernst & Young awarded him its Entrepreneur of the Year prize in 1998.

His second major venture, Venda, was founded in 1998 and later became the European market leader in on-demand retail eCommerce before its sale to Oracle in 2014. Rezolve's current management page said Venda ran major retail sites including Lands' End, Tesco, Boohoo, TJX Companies and Neiman Marcus. [Rezolve Management Team](https://investor.rezolve.com/corporate-governance/management-team) Alongside Venda, Wagner co-founded Attraqt in 2003, a search-and-merchandising platform for online retailers that listed on AIM in 2014 and which Wagner chaired until June 2016.

## The Powa chapter and its aftermath

No account of Wagner's biography that meets the Financial Times standard can omit Powa Technologies. Official UK records show that Powa Technologies Group plc entered administration on 19 February 2016, and the officers register for Powa Technologies Limited shows Daniel Wagner and several other directors resigning the same day. [Companies House – Powa insolvency](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/08389133/insolvency) [Companies House – Powa officers](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/06376989/officers) Later Rezolve disclosures did not revisit that episode in any detail: the 2024 Form 20-F described Wagner's earlier career around MAID and Venda rather than Powa. [Rezolve 2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm) That omission did not invalidate the current business, but it did leave investors to bridge an obvious gap in the founder narrative from the public record.

## Founding Rezolve and the SPAC path

Wagner founded Rezolve AI Limited in June 2016, less than six months after Powa's collapse, incorporating the company in England and Wales. [The 2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm) records that foundation date as the formal start of his tenure as CEO and director.

The original product was mobile image and audio recognition technology that made advertising shoppable via smartphone — a narrower brief than the Brain Suite. Rezolve repositioned around generative-AI retail capabilities as the LLM wave crested in 2022–2023, culminating in the August 2024 NASDAQ listing via Armada Acquisition Corp. I. Wagner retained the roles of Founder, CEO, and Chairman through the merger.



## Board composition

Following the SPAC merger, Rezolve initially adopted a classified board. Post-closing disclosures listed Daniel Wagner and John Wagner as Class III directors; Anthony Sharp, Sir David Wright, Stephen Perry and Derek Smith as Class II directors; and Stephen Herbert, the Armada sponsor representative, as the sole Class I director. [Rezolve Aug. 2024 post-combination filing](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/7701/html)

By the frozen snapshot, that board had changed materially. Rezolve said in a 15 August 2025 6-K that Stephen Herbert had ceased to be a director when the sponsor's nomination right expired, and an October 10, 2025 share-transfer release referred to the estate of the late John Wagner. [Rezolve Aug. 15 2025 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/7886/html) [Rezolve Oct. 10 2025 release](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-plc-announces-shareholder-transfer-new-global)

The current investor-relations board page, last accessible within the frozen window, listed five directors: Daniel M. Wagner as chairman and chief executive, Anthony Sharp as non-executive deputy chairman, Sir David Wright, Dr. Steve Perry and Dr. Derek Smith. Wright chaired the audit committee, Perry chaired compensation, and Smith chaired nominating and corporate governance. [Rezolve Board of Directors](https://investor.rezolve.com/corporate-governance/board-of-directors)

No Tether representative held a board seat in those current board disclosures, and no board observer right was described in any SEC filing or investor-relations communication located within the frozen window. The Tether relationship remained commercial and financial rather than governance-based. [Rezolve Board of Directors](https://investor.rezolve.com/corporate-governance/board-of-directors)

The combination of chairman and chief executive remained with Daniel Wagner, but by May 2026 the company also had a disclosed non-executive deputy chairman and three separate committee chairs, which made the governance picture more structured than the immediate post-SPAC board table suggested.

## The executive team: constitution and evolution

At the August 2024 NASDAQ listing, the operating leadership team consisted of:

**Richard Burchill, CFO** — Joined in September 2021. Listing-era disclosures described him as CFO after an earlier period as Group Finance Director; the current management page said he had spent 21 years at Arcadia Group, including 16 years as Director of Treasury, Card Services and Payment. [Rezolve Aug. 2024 post-combination filing](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/7701/html) [Rezolve Management Team](https://investor.rezolve.com/corporate-governance/management-team)

**Sauvik Banerjjee, CEO Products, Technology & Digital Services** — Joined in August 2022. Listing-era disclosures described him as founding CTO of TataCLiQ and a founding team member at Tata Digital and Tata Neu; the current management page still anchored his background in Tata Group, SAP and Accenture. [Rezolve Aug. 2024 post-combination filing](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/7701/html) [Rezolve Management Team](https://investor.rezolve.com/corporate-governance/management-team)

**Peter Vesco, Chief Commercial Officer and GM EMEA** — Joined in March 2020. The management page described prior roles including CEO of ClickandBuy and SVP at Deutsche Telekom Payments. [Rezolve Management Team](https://investor.rezolve.com/corporate-governance/management-team)

**Arthur Yao, Deputy CEO** — Rezolve's public materials positioned him as the executive bridging AI strategy, operations and partner-channel economics before his later promotion to COFO. [Rezolve Management Team](https://investor.rezolve.com/corporate-governance/management-team)

By the frozen snapshot, the current management page showed that the company had thickened that bench materially. In addition to Wagner, Yao, Burchill, Banerjjee and Vesco, Rezolve was publicly presenting Crispin Lowery as Chief Revenue Officer, Roland Gossage as Chief Growth Officer and Dr. Salman Ahmad as Chief Scientist. The change mattered because it showed a company trying to move from founder-centric product evangelism to a more segmented operating model: revenue, growth, science, finance and professional services were all being given named executive owners rather than sitting inside a single product-and-founder narrative. [Rezolve Management Team](https://investor.rezolve.com/corporate-governance/management-team)

## The October 2025 reorganisation

On 22 October 2025, Wagner announced a sweeping reshuffle described as marking "a pivotal step as the company transitions from early-stage growth to disciplined operational scale." The restructuring had four principal effects.

Arthur Yao expanded his brief from Deputy CEO to **Chief Operating and Financial Officer (COFO)**, absorbing both global operations and financial stewardship under a single executive. Richard Burchill stepped back to Group Finance Director, a narrower reporting role. **Crispin Lowery** was appointed Chief Revenue Officer, tasked with building a global enterprise sales organisation. **Roland Gossage** — a prior executive whose background spans retail-search and digital-commerce platforms — transitioned to **Chief Growth Officer**, bridging product evolution and market development. **Salman Ahmed** moved to the role of **Chief Scientist**, leading Rezolve's AI Lab and its planned AI Academy. Sauvik Banerjjee was subsequently repositioned as **President, Global Professional Services and Chief Digital Officer**, indicating a commercial services layer being built around the Brain Suite product. [Rezolve leadership update](https://rezolve.com/press-releases/rezolve-ai-strengthens-leadership-team-to-accelerate-global-growth-operational-scale-and-ai-innovation/) [Rezolve Management Team](https://investor.rezolve.com/corporate-governance/management-team)

> "Rezolve is entering its most exciting chapter yet. These leadership appointments align our organization for scale, discipline, and innovation as we continue to deliver against our growth ambitions… With Arthur, Richard, Crispin, Roland, Salman, and Sauvik leading their respective disciplines, Rezolve now has the executive firepower to deliver operational excellence, sustained growth, and category-defining innovation." — Daniel M. Wagner, 22 October 2025

The restructuring effectively replaced a product-centric CTO-anchored structure with a dual-track model: Yao driving operational and financial discipline while Lowery and Gossage build the commercial engine. Whether that configuration can convert the partner-led pipeline into recurring revenue — the central question for RZLV through 2026 and 2027 — depends as much on Wagner's judgement in delegating as on the credentials of his new hires. His track record shows he can attract institutional-grade talent. Holding them, and translating their output into durable enterprise contracts, is the variable that the Powa chapter left unresolved and that the post-SPAC years at Rezolve will ultimately adjudicate.

The same point applied to the board. By May 2026 the disclosed governance structure was no longer simply Wagner plus the remnants of the SPAC architecture; it was a smaller board with separate committee chairs, a disclosed deputy chairman, and a management team that had visibly broadened beneath the founder. Whether that was enough independence and operating depth for a company trying simultaneously to scale software revenue, integrate acquisitions and manage an unusually active capital structure was left to the market's judgement, but the public record did at least show a more institutional shape than the listing-era materials alone suggested.

---

**Sources:** [Rezolve 2024 Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm) · [Rezolve IR – Board of Directors](https://investor.rezolve.com/corporate-governance/board-of-directors) · [Rezolve IR – Management Team](https://investor.rezolve.com/corporate-governance/management-team) · [Rezolve leadership update, Oct. 22 2025](https://rezolve.com/press-releases/rezolve-ai-strengthens-leadership-team-to-accelerate-global-growth-operational-scale-and-ai-innovation/) · [Rezolve Aug. 15 2025 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/7886/html) · [Rezolve Oct. 10 2025 share-transfer release](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-plc-announces-shareholder-transfer-new-global) · [Companies House – Powa insolvency](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/08389133/insolvency) · [Companies House – Powa officers](https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/06376989/officers)

chapters.title: Microsoft, Google, Tether plus the retail and quick-service-restaurant customer base
chapters.body:
## The Platform, Not the Pipe: A Partner-Led Distribution Thesis

Rezolve's commercial strategy rested on a single architectural bet: that three hyperscale partners — Microsoft, Google, and Tether — could place the Brain Suite in front of large retailers at a speed and scale that a direct salesforce could never match. By Q1 2026, the thesis had passed its first credibility test. The question remained whether a customer base that Rezolve itself described as more than 950 enterprise clients would convert with the velocity that $360 million of 2026 revenue guidance required. [FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html) [Q1 2026 update](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-delivers-60-million-q1-2026-revenue-exceeding-full/)

## Microsoft: Five Years, Thirty-Five Thousand Sellers

The first pillar went live on [October 3, 2024](https://news.microsoft.com/source/2024/10/03/microsoft-and-rezolve-ai-partner-to-drive-global-retail-innovation-with-ai-powered-commerce-solutions/), when Rezolve and Microsoft announced a five-year strategic partnership to drive AI-powered retail innovation through the Azure cloud. The commercial architecture was direct: Rezolve's Brain Suite — Brain Commerce, Brain Checkout, and Brain Assistant — would be hosted on Microsoft Azure, listed on the Azure Marketplace for seamless global procurement, and sold through co-sell arrangements with approximately 35,000 incentivised Microsoft field sellers. Access to the ISV Success Benefits programme through the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program came as a further structural support, alongside commitments to joint marketing campaigns, technical enablement, and public-relations activity.

For Rezolve, the economics of that co-sell fleet were the essential point. Building a direct salesforce capable of consistently reaching top-100 global retailers takes years and hundreds of millions in operating spend. Routing Brain Suite through a partner with pre-existing enterprise relationships — relationships in which Azure was already the infrastructure of record — compressed that timeline, at least structurally.

Nick Parker, Microsoft's President of Industry and Partnerships, characterised the joint proposition as bringing "a differentiated conversational AI experience to our mutual customers."

The 2024 [Form 20-F](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm) filed with the SEC acknowledged the dependency candidly, noting that Rezolve expected to be materially reliant on its Microsoft agreement in North America and Europe. That disclosure confirmed the partnership's structural centrality while flagging concentration risk if the co-sell commitments did not translate into contracted recurring revenue.

## Google Cloud: Reseller, Infrastructure Provider, and Potential Amplifier

Seven weeks after the Microsoft announcement, on [November 20, 2024](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-and-google-sign-strategic-partnership-revolutionize/), Rezolve moved to secure the second hyperscale pillar. The Google Cloud partnership was structurally more aggressive in one dimension: Google Cloud would act as an active **reseller** of Brain Suite globally, not merely a marketplace host. A resell arrangement puts Google's own sales incentives behind Rezolve's revenue line in a way that a marketplace listing alone does not.

The companies' joint disclosure projected that Google's sales channel would account for more than 50 percent of Rezolve's forecasted revenues over "the next several years" — an extraordinary projection given the scale of revenues the company was guiding toward. Customers deploying Rezolve through the Google channel were offered the further inducement of applying solution costs against existing Google Cloud committed-use agreements, effectively reducing the incremental procurement friction for enterprises already under multi-year Google contracts.

The partnership also opened longer-term optionality that attracted limited analyst attention at the time: Rezolve's technology was placed in scope for assessment by Google engineers examining potential integration with Search, Maps, Android, and YouTube — four of the highest-traffic commercial surfaces the company operates. Whether any of those evaluations progressed to production arrangements within the frozen window of 2026-05-23 was not confirmed in public disclosures.



## Tether: Stablecoin Commerce and a Strategic Stake

The third relationship brought a different asset class to the table. On [4 December 2024](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/tether-and-rezolve-ai-share-vision-make-crypto-mainstream), Rezolve announced the integration of Tether's open-source Wallet Development Kit (WDK) into its Brain Checkout platform, enabling consumers to pay with USDT, Bitcoin, and other digital assets at participating merchants while retailers received settlement in fiat currency — eliminating traditional interchange and merchant-processing fees in the process. Rezolve described the Tether relationship as a strategic partnership with an equity dimension, though the precise size of any Tether shareholding was not publicly itemised in filings available through the frozen window.

As evidence of consumer appetite for crypto-denominated commerce, Rezolve cited its own operations in Brazil, where it said it had already processed more than $1 billion in USDT and Bitcoin transactions through its payments infrastructure — a figure it presented as proof-of-concept for a model that remained largely theoretical in major developed markets. [Rezolve stablecoin rollout update](https://rezolve.com/press-releases/rezolve-ai-accelerates-global-stablecoin-payments-rollout-to-power-the-next-wave-of-agentic-commerce/)

The partnership acquired a further regulatory dimension in 2025, when [Tether announced USAT](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-set-power-next-gen-retail-payments-tether-unveils), a U.S.-compliant stablecoin structured around the requirements of the GENIUS Act. For Rezolve's Brain Checkout layer, USAT opened the path toward a regulated crypto-payments product in the American market — previously constrained by regulatory ambiguity — without requiring Rezolve to build or maintain its own digital-asset infrastructure.

Wagner called the USAT launch a validation of the original thesis: "The announcement of USAT under the GENIUS Act validates exactly what we set out to do with Tether by bringing regulated, frictionless crypto payments into mainstream commerce."

## The Customer Roster: From Drive-Through to Delhi

The three partnership rails were means, not ends. What they were designed to accelerate was signed, revenue-generating relationships with large operators in retail, grocery, quick-service restaurants, and digital marketplaces.

By [February 2025](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-kicks-2025-major-retail-expansion-leading-brands/), Rezolve disclosed a named customer list that spanned geographies and formats. In the quick-service restaurant segment, **Dunkin'** deployed the Brain Suite's Mobile SDK for drive-through detection, enabling automated order pickup and personalised digital menu board experiences — a use case that married Brain Engage's location intelligence with Brain Checkout's payment orchestration. **Philz Coffee**, the California-founded specialty chain, rolled out contactless pickup solutions through the same SDK stack.

In physical retail, **BJ's Wholesale Club** integrated geolocation-powered curbside pickup with differentiated in-app experiences. **Discount Tire**, the largest independent tyre retailer in the United States by outlet count, deployed AI-driven geolocation for automated appointment check-in, reducing customer service dwell times. **Coles Supermarkets**, one of Australia's two dominant grocery operators with more than 1,800 outlets, activated contactless grocery pickup. The **Phoenix Suns** NBA franchise used location-based marketing for in-stadium visitors.

The digital-commerce layer grew heavier with Indian and Latin American names. **AJIO**, the Reliance Retail-owned fashion marketplace, renewed and upsold its Rezolve deployment as of [late 2025](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-accelerates-global-momentum-live-enterprise). **Snapdeal**, ranked among India's top-five online marketplaces, signed a multi-year agreement covering multi-search and AI-driven product recommendations. **VogaCloset**, the MENA-focused fashion platform based in the United Kingdom, went live with conversational commerce; by the December 2025 update, 60 percent of its shoppers were actively using image-upload product search. In Latin America, **GAP** and **Banana Republic** in Mexico deployed Brain Commerce for multilingual semantic search and SEO enrichment, while **Liverpool**, the leading Mexican department store group, sustained what Rezolve described as a multi-year flagship relationship. Qatar Airways was in advanced commercial discussions as of the December 2025 update, signalling expansion into travel and hospitality verticals.

## Platform Scale

By end-2025, the platform reached 59.8 million consumer devices, processed 112.7 billion API calls, and logged 306.7 million physical-to-digital geofence triggers across more than 950 enterprise clients. Core software gross margins exceeded 90 percent on a blended GAAP margin of 66 percent. [FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html)

> "When retailers move from search to conversation, engagement increases, conversion improves and customers stay longer. These wins are not pilots or experiments, they are live, enterprise-grade deployments that we believe validate Rezolve as the AI commerce layer for global brands."
> — Daniel Wagner, December 2025

---

**Sources:** [Microsoft-Rezolve partnership announcement (Microsoft Source, Oct. 2024)](https://news.microsoft.com/source/2024/10/03/microsoft-and-rezolve-ai-partner-to-drive-global-retail-innovation-with-ai-powered-commerce-solutions/) · [Google-Rezolve partnership (Rezolve IR, Nov. 2024)](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-and-google-sign-strategic-partnership-revolutionize/) · [Tether / Brain Checkout announcement (Rezolve IR, Dec. 2024)](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/tether-and-rezolve-ai-share-vision-make-crypto-mainstream) · [Retail expansion release (Rezolve IR, Feb. 2025)](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-kicks-2025-major-retail-expansion-leading-brands/) · [Liverpool Mexico contract (Rezolve IR, Apr. 2025)](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-secures-98-million-annual-contract-liverpool-mexico) · [December 2025 enterprise deployments (Rezolve IR)](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-accelerates-global-momentum-live-enterprise) · [FY2025 results / March 2026 6-K](https://investor.rezolve.com/node/8791/html) · [Q1 2026 update](https://investor.rezolve.com/news-releases/news-release-details/rezolve-ai-delivers-60-million-q1-2026-revenue-exceeding-full/) · [RZLV Form 20-F FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001920294/000095017025057622/rzlv-20241231.htm)

chapters.title: Where Rezolve sits against Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Shopify, Adobe Commerce, and broader retail-AI platforms
chapters.body:
## A Different Level of the Stack

The commerce-technology landscape that Rezolve AI enters as a public company in August 2024 is already stratified by well-capitalised incumbents operating at distinct layers of the retail stack. Salesforce Commerce Cloud — built on the Demandware acquisition and now embedded in the broader Einstein and Agentforce AI ecosystem — claims deployments across more than 6,000 global brands and commands enterprise licence budgets that routinely reach seven figures annually. Shopify has remade the economics of mid-market retail through its unified payments-and-platform flywheel, with gross merchandise volume exceeding $235 billion in fiscal 2023 and a market capitalisation that briefly surpassed $100 billion in the post-pandemic boom. Adobe Commerce, inherited from the 2018 Magento acquisition, anchors the customisation-intensive segment of large enterprise. And commercetools, a MACH-architecture (Microservices, API-first, Cloud-native, Headless) pioneer out of Munich, has won fast-growing enterprise mandates from retailers that want composability over monolithic lock-in.

Rezolve's answer is structural rather than frontal. The Brain Suite is presented not as a competing commerce stack but as a generative-AI capability layer designed to sit above whatever platform a retailer already operates. Where Salesforce sells the operating system of the store, Rezolve sells the cognitive layer. This distinction is the company's clearest competitive argument and, measured against a landscape where every major platform is simultaneously building its own AI, its most consequential long-run bet.

## Against the Established Commerce Platforms

Salesforce's Einstein GPT and the subsequent Agentforce rollout represent the most direct incumbent response to the generative-AI commerce opportunity. Salesforce can bundle AI capabilities into existing Commerce Cloud contracts — a natural expansion sale that requires no new vendor relationship, new security review, or new integration project on the retailer's part. The bundle advantage is formidable: Salesforce's retail customers are already on the platform, already paying, and already familiar with the administrative interface. Rezolve's counter-argument, implicit in its partner-led go-to-market, is that generative-AI commerce is specialised enough to justify a best-of-breed overlay even for Salesforce shops — and that Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud, both of which have their own commercial relationships with Salesforce's enterprise customers, provide a distribution vector to reach those buyers through a trusted channel.

Shopify presents a structurally different competitive dynamic. Its 2023 rollout of Shopify Magic (AI-assisted copy, image, and product description generation) and the subsequent Sidekick merchant assistant mark a clear intention to own the generative layer for the several-million merchants on its platform. But Shopify's centre of gravity remains SMB-to-lower-enterprise: Rezolve's stated target of large retailers and top-100 global brands sits above Shopify's natural hunting ground, and the Brain Suite's emphasis on complex checkout orchestration and loyalty is calibrated for retailers whose transaction complexity and basket sizes justify dedicated AI spend that Shopify's margin-compressed subscription model cannot easily serve.

Adobe Commerce, running on Adobe Experience Cloud's broader data and personalisation infrastructure, is the most technically customisable of the major platforms and therefore the one most likely to coexist with an AI overlay like Brain Suite rather than resist it. Adobe's Firefly generative model and Sensei AI capabilities are advancing, but Adobe Commerce deployments are notoriously implementation-heavy — they tend to run on systems-integrator timelines measured in months, which arguably creates an opening for modular AI layers that can be contracted and deployed more quickly. commercetools, similarly, operates at the API layer and is by design composable, making it a natural complement to Brain Suite rather than a zero-sum competitor.

## Against Retail-AI Point Solutions

The more granular competitive threat comes from a cohort of AI-native point-solution vendors that have established themselves in specific segments of the retail stack. Bloomreach combines content management, product discovery, and marketing automation under its Loomi AI engine, with a customer roster that includes retailers such as Marks & Spencer and Bosch. Algolia, with an approximate private valuation of $2.25 billion at its last disclosed round, dominates AI-powered site search and has extended into recommendations and personalisation. Constructor focuses on enterprise product discovery — search, browse, recommendations, quiz — for large-scale retailers that want algorithmic precision in catalogue navigation. Coveo brings enterprise search and AI-driven experience capabilities that overlap substantially with Brain Commerce's semantic search positioning.

Against each of these, Rezolve's differentiating claim is breadth. Brain Suite is presented as a unified generative layer spanning discovery, checkout, and engagement — the argument being that a retailer running Algolia for search, a separate checkout optimisation vendor, and a third loyalty platform is managing three integration surfaces and three commercial relationships where Brain Suite nominally provides one. The thesis echoes the platform-versus-best-of-breed debate that has recurred in enterprise software for decades, and it carries the same risk: a bundled product that is excellent at none of its components loses to specialised competition on every front. The company's 2024–2025 disclosures do not provide enough granular product-benchmark data for an external observer to resolve that question definitively.

Lily AI represents a narrower but instructive case. Its product-attribute enrichment technology helps retailers improve product discoverability by automatically tagging catalogue items with consumer-language attributes. It is a genuine AI-native solution with demonstrated retailer deployments, but it operates at a single layer of the stack — a useful illustration of the growing specialisation within retail AI and the difficulty of sustaining a multi-module Brain Suite positioning against focused competitors that each own one problem deeply.

## The Hyperscaler Dimension: Partners and Shadow Competitors

The most structurally complex element of Rezolve's competitive positioning is its hyperscaler relationships.
